love.name: Tyler Love
love.intro: Everything on rodenlaw.com that needs a Georgia lawyer's read, in one place. Tap a button on each card; your answers save as you go, and you can stop and come back from the same link. When you're done, press Send at the bottom.

sections.title: Georgia law-pack sign-off
sections.intro: Each card is one statement of Georgia law the site may make, with the authority it rests on. Once you sign a statement, new content may rely on it and the site check measures every page against it. Until then we publish no new Georgia legal claim. Approve, or give the wording you want; a correction comes back to you once more before it counts. "Approve all" on a group is fine.

groups.title: A. Authorities already cited across the site (33)
B. Authorities checked against the statute text, not yet signed (16)

items.title: Troubled-teen abuse page
items.question: Should the page mention that § 9-3-33.1 claims against an institution need more proof than claims against the abuser?

items.title: Troubled-teen abuse page
items.question: Most of these facilities are outside Georgia. Does Roden refer those cases out, or co-counsel? The FAQ wording on where a survivor can bring a claim depends on your answer.

sections.title: Corrections that change what a page says the law is
sections.intro: Each card shows what the page says now and the wording we propose. None of these is live. Our Georgia text was read from FindLaw copies current to early 2024 (two sections only to 2021), so please check for any 2024–2026 act, especially on e-scooters, PTVs and golf carts.

items.title: Brain-injury tolling sentence
items.question: Post 1840 has a sentence on tolling for a traumatic brain injury under § 9-3-90. Is it right as written? If not, what should it say?

items.title: E-scooter intersection page: negligence per se
items.question: We removed the claim that a Georgia e-scooter statute governs these crashes. Does the next sentence's negligence-per-se point still stand without a scooter statute?

items.title: Golf-cart pedestrian page: the rules-of-the-road hook
items.question: We dropped § 40-6-330 as the source of a PTV driver's duty to follow the rules of the road. Should the page cite § 40-6-91 (or something else) instead, or stay uncited?

items.title: Pre-suit offers: the bill number
items.question: Post 1722 now says § 9-11-67.1 was "amended in 2024, for offers made on or after April 22, 2024" (from the section's history line). What is the bill number, if you'd like it named?

sections.title: Wording already changed on live pages
sections.intro: These went live on 10-24 because the old sentence was plainly wrong. They change wording, not just a citation, so they need your yes.

sections.title: Two abuse-survivor deadlines to sign
sections.intro: You signed the South Carolina statements in September. These two are new. Once signed, new content may rely on them. The troubled-teen abuse page's FAQ now uses general deadline wording; a more specific version waits on these two.

items.title: Troubled-teen abuse page
items.question: Most of these facilities are outside South Carolina. Does Roden refer those cases out, or co-counsel?

items.title: Troubled-teen abuse page: Rule 7.1 / 7.2
items.question: The page says "history of proven results", calls the firm's experience "decades", uses "knowledgeable" and "experienced", and has five no-fee lines that say nothing about case costs. Is any of it a problem in South Carolina, and what wording do you want instead?

sections.title: Corrections that change what a page says the law is
sections.intro: Each card shows what the page says now and the wording we propose. None of these is live.

items.title: Comparative fault: joint and several liability

pairs.now: "A defendant found to be more than 50% at fault may be held jointly and severally liable for economic damages"
pairs.proposed: "A defendant found to be 50% or more at fault may be held jointly and severally liable" (S.C. Code § 15-38-15)

items.question: Should "for economic damages" stay? Your pack entry for § 15-38-15 carries no economic-only limit, but we haven't checked that point. (The page's key takeaway was already corrected on 10-24.)

sections.title: Wording on the pedestrian pages, held for you

items.title: Walking along a highway

pairs.now: Use the sidewalk; otherwise walk on the left side facing traffic.
pairs.proposed: "Use a sidewalk when one is available, otherwise the shoulder, and walk on the left side facing traffic only where there is neither."

items.question: § 56-5-3160(b)–(c) puts the shoulder before the left-side rule. Is the proposed wording right?

items.title: Crosswalk yield duty
items.question: The page now quotes § 56-5-3130(a) in full, but its "critical elements" bullets and FAQ 0 still state the yield duty without the condition "when traffic-control signals are not in place or not in operation". Should we add that condition there?

items.title: The "notwithstanding" gloss
items.question: The page reads § 56-5-3230's "notwithstanding" as overriding every other provision. The statute says "notwithstanding other provisions of any local ordinance". Should the gloss be narrowed to local ordinances?

items.title: Cyclists' equal rights
items.question: Two cycling pages (posts 4172, 4173) cite § 56-5-3435 for cyclists having the same rights as drivers. We've only verified that section for the passing distance. Is it the right cite for equal rights? If not, which section is?

items.title: Guilty pleas as evidence
items.question: Pages citing § 56-5-6160 carve out guilty pleas from the bar on using traffic convictions as evidence, relying on Samuel v. Mouzon. Is that right?

items.title: Troubled-teen FAQ: general deadline wording (live since 10-24)

pairs.now: A claim that abuse survivors generally get extended deadlines.
pairs.proposed: "It may not be too late, but some claims may already have expired. Filing deadlines depend on the kind of claim and the state where it is filed, and they are strict."

items.question: Is the general wording acceptable until the two deadlines above are signed?
